title: 005 — Concepts as keys, hierarchies as digits: bag and tree nearness together

sections.title: P1 — bag similarity exactly: one attribute per key
labels: one attribute per key: count exact

findings.label: P1
findings.value: with one attribute per key the shared-attribute count is exact for every pair; 004's boundary was the encoding (all attributes in one value), not the memory

sections.title: P2–P3 — bag and tree together, against MAP-I

legend.map_acc: per-attribute depth after clean-up against that attribute's 27 leaves in both records

findings.label: P2–P3
findings.value: one subtraction gives every attribute's depth of agreement, exactly, covering bag (shared concepts) and tree (shared ancestry) at once; MAP-I matches it only at n = 10,000 with a clean-up per role

sections.title: P4 — frequent concepts on small primes is Huffman-like

legend.order: frequency: most frequent attribute → smallest prime

findings.label: P4
findings.value: giving frequent concepts the smallest primes cuts the size of sparse records to about 0.6× a random assignment: frequent concepts get the cheapest keys, as a Huffman code gives frequent symbols the shortest words
